vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: cmic-skill-scanner-linux-amd64
Version: 0.6.4

The skill includes a pre-compiled Linux binary (assets/bin/skillscan) which is opaque and cannot be audited within the skill bundle. While its stated purpose is security scanning, the INSTALL.md file documents a feature to upload scan reports to external servers via the '--upload-url' flag. This capability, combined with the execution of binary code, presents a risk for data exfiltration if the agent is directed to use a malicious endpoint, although no hardcoded malicious URLs or clear evidence of intent were found.

llm.summary: The skill claims to provide a Linux x64 scanner binary and instructions to run it, but the package lacks the claimed binary and its docs show an optional report-upload feature that could exfiltrate scanned content — the pieces are internally inconsistent and deserve caution.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and INSTALL.md describe a native binary at assets/bin/skillscan and give SHA-256, usage, and release links. However the package manifest and provided files do not include the binary itself (only SKILL.md, INSTALL.md, agents/openai.yaml, and build-info.json are present). That mismatch (documented binary vs. missing artifact) is incoherent: either the package omitted the binary or the skill advertises capabilities it doesn't include. The repository link (gitee) exists but the skill package does not automatically include or fetch a binary, which is unexpected for a 'binary included' claim.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions are mostly confined to scanning skill source files and verifying checksums locally. However INSTALL.md documents an --upload-url parameter and explicitly states the upload payload contains embedded review details (full scan summary and findings). That means if the (claimed) binary is used with upload features, scanned skill contents could be transmitted to external endpoints. The SKILL.md asserts it analyzes target skill code 'not your system', but the docs also say the scanner flags patterns like access to ~/.ssh or ~/.aws — which is reasonable as detection rules but highlights that the scanner might identify credentials in scanned packages. Overall the instructions don't tell the agent to read unrelated system state, but they do describe an optional path that transmits scan results externally.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec in the registry entry (instruction-only), yet the package documentation repeatedly refers to a bundled binary. Because the binary file is absent from the provided manifest, there is no built-in install mechanism to obtain a verified executable. The upstream repository and releases are on Gitee; downloading a binary from an external release is possible but would execute arbitrary native code from an external host. The package expects local checksum verification, but the missing artifact plus reliance on an external release location increases risk and ambiguity.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, credentials, or config paths. That aligns with its stated purpose (a scanner that examines skill source files). However, the documented upload feature (--upload-url) would transmit scan output to an external endpoint if used, so while env/credential requests are proportionate, users should be aware of possible data exfiltration vectors if they opt into remote upload.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request persistent presence (always:false) and does not declare actions that modify system or other skills' configuration. It is user-invocable and allows autonomous invocation by default (normal). There is no evidence it attempts to elevate privileges or write persistent config.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Do not run or install anything until you resolve the missing-binary mismatch. Before proceeding: 1) Confirm whether assets/bin/skillscan is actually bundled — the package currently lacks the binary it documents. 2) If you obtain the binary from the linked Gitee releases, download it yourself, verify the SHA-256 against the project's official release files, and run it inside a sandboxed environment (VM or container). 3) Avoid using the --upload-url option unless you trust the destination — upload will include full scan details and could leak skill source code. 4) Prefer source builds or audit the upstream repository first; ask the publisher why the package claims a bundled binary but doesn't include it. If you can't verify provenance and checksum, treat the binary as untrusted.
